image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Large rectangular moulded plastic wheelie bin, a four-sided box-shaped tub clearly wider than it is tall and flat-sided, not round, its four flat panels tapering slightly inward toward the base with broad shallow ribs moulded down them and a moulded grip rail running along the back below the rim, closed by one wide flat rectangular lid hinged along the back top edge and overhanging the front rim as a thick lip, and underneath four swivel castors on short square pedestals, one at each corner, each castor a solid wheel in a plain U-shaped fork Materials: Dark green polyethylene chalky and sun-bleached across the lid and the upper front panel, grey and black scuffs along both ends where it has been dragged, dark grease and leachate staining down the front below the rim and pooled around the castor pedestals, a faded white stencilled panel on the front.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Rebuild 2026-08-31. Width corrected 1.37 -> 0.94 m against the Meshy band table and an independent 3/4 plate read, which agree at width/depth 1.23 and 1.19 against the build's 1.76; mean |delta width| 0.34 -> 0.0235 with no band left over the 0.12 flag. Rib pilasters rebuilt as single tapered prisms after a straight box and then a four-box stack both failed visibly on a leaning wall. Lid rebuilt as a two-step overhanging form with a raised centre panel and corner grip ribbing. Castors enlarged, front lugs added. 796/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries; turntable passes at all four azimuths with no holes and check-coplanar is clean.

featureReviews.evidence: A flat-sided rectangular tub tapering inward toward the base, 0.94 x 1.22 x 0.78 m, standing on four castors.
featureReviews.notes: WIDTH CORRECTED from 1.37 m to 0.94 m. The declaration was a list-time estimate and made the bin half again as wide as it should be against its own depth. The Meshy proxy's band table read width/height 0.65-0.76 across bands 2-9 against the build's 0.94-1.09 -- eight of ten bands over the 0.12 flag, mean |delta width| 0.34 -- while reading DEPTH at 0.50-0.62 against the build's 0.55-0.64, already right. An error in ONE axis is a declaration error, not a scale one. The plate agrees independently: read as a 3/4 view at ~30 degrees yaw its front face spans ~620 px and its side ~300, so true width/depth is (620/cos30)/(300/sin30) = 1.19, against the proxy's 1.23 and the build's 1.76. After the correction the band table reads mean |delta width| 0.0235 and mean |delta depth| 0.0540, with NO band over the flag.

featureReviews.evidence: Five moulded channels up each long wall, running from 0.22 m to 0.88 m and stopping below the rim so the two front lugs sit clear above them.
featureReviews.notes: THE WALL TAPERS, SO A STRAIGHT BOX CANNOT SIT ON IT, and that -- not the amount of relief -- is why these read as scratches before. The old build placed one box per rib at the wall depth of its own MIDPOINT, so each rib was buried in the wall over its top half and standing off it over the bottom half, rendering as a fin with a step in it that stopped short at both ends. A stack of four short boxes was tried next and is worse: it steps by the full taper per segment, 18 mm here, which renders as an unmistakable staircase, and more segments only makes the staircase finer. They are single tapered prisms now (Soup.wallRib), whose outer face is parallel to the wall by construction. Relief also doubled, 12 mm to 26 mm.

featureReviews.evidence: A two-step lid overhanging the body by 35 mm all round, with a raised centre panel and five-bar diagonal grip ribbing at each of the four corners; its own node, hinged along the rear top edge.
featureReviews.notes: It was a plain slab with one thin strip, which reads as a closed box rather than as a lid. The plate shows a stepped lid with a clear shadow gap under its edge on every side, a large centre panel inside a raised border, and diagonal grip ribbing at the corners -- which is most of what identifies a bin lid seen from above, and this prop is nearly always seen from above in a level. The centre panel and the grip bars both stand PROUD rather than being sunk: sunk, their top faces would share the lid top's plane facing the same way and tear into interleaved triangles as the camera moves.

featureReviews.evidence: Four swivel castors at the corners, wheel radius raised from 0.075 to 0.085 m, carrying the tub clear of the ground.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged in construction; enlarged so the undercarriage is legible at prop distance, where it was previously four dark specks. The forks stay schematic -- at 2 draw calls and 2 materials for this class there is no budget for a jointed castor and no distance at which it would be seen.

featureReviews.evidence: Moulded plastic at #5c7d62, measured #46624c and lifted to luma 118 with saturation held above 0.26.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged. The measurement is lifted because a side-lit face renders at ~0.56 of its painted luma, which would land the measured value at 51 against the harness backdrop's 58 and read as a hole; saturation is held so the prop clears the gate on chroma as well as value.
